# Volume 1 — CHAPTER XIV. Nell’s Confession

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

UPON the evening of Monday preceding the picnic, Thirza emerged from her room displaying a distressed expression.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0000 }

“Nell,” she uttered to the tiny individual, who was removing peas from their pods beside the immaculate table while performing “Nelly of the Hazel Dell” with an energy and feeling that reflected well on Isolde’s instruction, “did you notice my amethyst brooch anywhere? I believed I placed it into my pincushion upon returning home from church last night, but it is nowhere to be found.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0001 }

“I—I observed it earlier today while you were absent at the Aid Society,” Nell remarked, somewhat deliberately. “As I was walking by your door, I noticed it resting on the cushion, which prompted me to step inside to examine it.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0002 }

“Was it touched by you?” Thirza asked severely.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0003 }

“Y-e-e-s,” Nell conceded, “I lifted it and attached it to my breast merely to observe the appearance it would make.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0004 }

“You were not supposed to act in such a manner. Meddling is extremely improper for a young girl. To begin with, you ought not to have entered my room, and furthermore, you ought not to have handled a brooch that was not yours. Where did you leave it?”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0005 }

“Oh, I placed it on top of the bureau again. It was on me for less than a minute. Honestly, interfering wasn't my intention, Thirza. Entering and putting on the brooch didn't strike me as forbidden; however, I now recognize my mistake, and I promise not to repeat it. I have that single virtue. A bad deed is something I never commit a second time.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0006 }

“It wasn't returned by you,” Thirza said. “The bureau doesn't have that brooch anywhere on it. Nell, you have taken it out or done something else to it.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0007 }

“Indeed I returned it,” Nell stated swiftly—with impudence, in Thirza’s view. “I cannot recall with certainty if I thrust it into the pincushion or placed it inside the porcelain dish. Nevertheless, I am absolutely sure that I returned it.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0008 }

“I will return and check once more,” Thirza said, deciding to be fair. “Should you have returned that brooch, it remains in that place. Should it be absent, I will be certain you failed to do so, nothing more!”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0009 }

Thirza proceeded to her bedroom and conducted an exhaustive hunt, searching not merely across the bureau but throughout all the additional spots where she imagined the brooch could conceivably be. She was unable to discover it, so she went back into the kitchen.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0010 }

“Nell, the brooch has disappeared. You admitted yourself that you were the final person who touched it. Now, where did you put it? Give me the true story immediately. Did you carry it outside and drop it?”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0011 }

“No, I didn’t,” Nell said with gravity, directly returning the furious look from Thirza. “The brooch was never taken from your room by me, and that is a fact, even were I to be brought to the block on account of it—even though I don’t really know what a block might be. So that is that, Thirza.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0012 }

Although Nell’s “so there” had been uttered merely to stress her claim, it was interpreted by Thirza as a sign of rebellion.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0013 }

“Nell, my belief is that you are speaking untruthfully to me,” she stated with sharpness. “My certainty is that you are. Look here, refrain from speaking further unless your intention is to disclose the entire truth. Retire to your chamber and remain within it until your readiness to admit everything arrives.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0014 }

“Shall I carry the peas along?” Nell inquired submissively.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0015 }

“No, I am going to complete shelling them on my own. Follow my instructions.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0016 }

After Nell left, Thirza performed her nightly chores feeling exceptionally unsettled. The fate of her precious brooch deeply troubled her. Had Nell perhaps dropped it somewhere? It seemed terribly deceitful for the young girl to disclaim taking the item, especially since it was blatantly obvious that she had done so. Furthermore, she had maintained such an unguilty expression while doing it!
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0017 }

“I do not know what I would not rather have occurred,” Thirza reflected, while she anxiously removed the peas from their pods. “Naturally, I do not believe she intended to commit a theft or anything of that sort. She has simply removed it to play with or to assist that imagination she has. It is obvious she took it, because nobody has been inside that room since she occupied it, according to her own account, until my visit this evening. And there is nothing more certain than that the brooch is missing. My assumption is that she lost it and fears admitting it out of dread of punishment. Contemplating that she utters lies is a terrible thing. That is a much worse matter than her outburst of anger. Carrying the responsibility of a child in your home whom you are unable to trust is fearful. What she has exhibited is deceit and dishonesty. I assert that I am more upset over that than over the brooch. Had she merely spoken the truth regarding it, I would not care nearly as much.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0018 }

At various points over the course of the evening, Thirza returned to her room to look for the brooch, yet she could not locate it. Going to the east gable at bedtime yielded nothing either. Even though Nell continuously claimed to have no knowledge of the brooch, Thirza merely became even more certain of her guilt.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0019 }

When the next morning arrived, she related the narrative to Obed. Obed found himself mystified and bewildered; although he was unable to abandon his belief in Nell so rapidly, he was forced to concede that the situation pointed toward her guilt.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0020 }

“Is there any chance it dropped in back of the bureau?” represented his sole possible idea.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0021 }

“I’ve shifted the bureau, removed the drawers, and searched through every single crevice,” Thirza answered with certainty. “The brooch has disappeared, taken by that child who then lied regarding it. That is the straightforward, unpleasant fact, Obed Abernethy, and we had better confront it squarely.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0022 }

“So, how do you plan to handle this?” asked Obed in a dejected manner, privately relieved that Thirza, rather than himself, was forced to manage the circumstances. On this occasion, he possessed no wish to meddle.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0023 }

“Until she confesses, she’ll stay in her room,” Thirza said grimly, recalling how well this strategy had worked in the previous instance. “We’ll see after that. If she’ll just say where she took the brooch, maybe we’ll be able to find it; but regardless, Obed, she’ll have to be severely punished.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0024 }

“Well now, she will need to be punished by you,” said Obed, as he reached toward his hat. “Remember that I am not involved in this. You were the one who warned me away.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0025 }

Abandonment was all that Thirza felt. Consulting Mrs. Sowerby for counsel was not even an option for her. Carrying an extremely grave expression, she walked up to the east gable, and she departed from it bearing an expression that was graver yet. Confessing was something Nell firmly declined to do. That she had not taken the brooch was what she continued to maintain. The youngster had clearly been weeping, inducing a sharp feeling of compassion in Thirza, though she forcefully held it back. Once night arrived, she found herself, to use her own words, “beat out.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0026 }

“You will remain inside this room until you admit it, Nell. Make up your mind to that,” she said firmly.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0027 }

“However, Thirza, the picnic takes place tomorrow,” Nell shouted. “Surely you will not prevent me from attending that? You will allow me to leave for just the afternoon, will you not? Following that, I will remain in this place with pleasure for any length of time you desire. Nevertheless, attending the picnic is something I must do.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0028 }

“You will not attend picnics or any other places prior to confessing, Nell.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0029 }

“Oh, Thirza,” Nell gasped.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0030 }

However, Thirza had departed and closed the door.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0031 }

The morning of Wednesday broke with a brightness and beauty that seemed tailored specifically for the outing. Surrounding Grey Shutters, birds trilled their songs; within the garden, the Madonna lilies released fragrance that swept through every doorway and window on invisible breezes, drifting like blessing spirits across the hallways and chambers. Down in the hollow, the birches swayed their hands merrily, as though waiting for the customary morning hello Nell offered from the eastern gable. However, Nell was absent from her window. Upon bringing her breakfast upstairs, Thirza discovered the girl perched stiffly atop her bed, white-faced and determined, her lips pressed firmly together and her eyes shining.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0032 }

“Thirza, I’m ready to confess.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0033 }

“Ah!” Set down by Thirza was her tray. Yet another time her approach proved effective; nevertheless, her accomplishment brought her deep bitterness. “Let me hear what you have to say then, Nell.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0034 }

“I took the amethyst brooch,” Nell stated, resembling someone reciting a memorized lesson. “Just like you described, I took it. Stealing it was not my intention upon entering. However, Thirza, once I fastened it onto my chest, it appeared so lovely that a powerful temptation conquered me. I pictured the utter thrill of bringing it along to Larkrise while pretending to be the Lady Lucinda Fitzgerald. Possessing an authentic amethyst brooch would make pretending to be the Lady Lucinda far simpler. Although Isolde and I craft necklaces using roseberries, how can roseberries compare with amethysts? Consequently, I stole the brooch. My intention was to return it prior to your arrival back home. To make the journey last longer, I traveled the entire distance by way of the road. While crossing the bridge spanning the Lake of Glassy Waters, I removed the brooch so that I might view it once more. Oh, the way it gleamed in the sun! Then, as I bent over the bridge, it simply slid right out of my fingers—like this—and plunged down—down—down, gleaming with purple flashes, until it submerged eternally under the Lake of Glassy Waters. And Thirza, that is the most thorough confession I am capable of making.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0035 }

A fresh wave of furious rage welled up in Thirza's heart. The young girl had appropriated and misplaced her cherished amethyst brooch, yet she remained seated there placidly detailing the particulars of the incident, showing no obvious remorse or regret whatsoever.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0036 }

“Nell, this is awful,” she remarked, attempting to keep her voice steady. “No girl I have ever known of is as thoroughly bad as you.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0037 }

“Yes, I believe I am,” Nell concurred placidly. “And I am aware that I must receive punishment. Performing that punishment will be your responsibility, Thirza. Won’t you kindly execute it immediately, as I wish to attend the picnic without any worries weigh upon me.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0038 }

“A picnic, of all things! Today will bring no picnic for you, Nell Harcourt. This is to be your penalty. Even so, it fails to be anywhere near harsh enough considering your actions!”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0039 }

“Refuse to attend the outing!” Nell leaped up and seized the hand of Thirza. “Yet your word was given that I could! Oh, Thirza, attending the outing is essential for me. My admission was made for that reason. Subject me to any penalty except that one. Oh, Thirza, I beg you, I beg you, permit me to attend the outing. Consider the ice cream! As far as you are aware, another opportunity to sample ice cream might never come my way.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0040 }

Without emotion, Thirza unclasped the hands of Nell that were holding onto her.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0041 }

“There is no need to beg, Nell. That’s final, and you are not attending the picnic. No, do not say a single word.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0042 }

Nell understood that Thirza could not be persuaded. Joining her hands, she uttered a sharp scream, after which she threw herself face down upon the bed, weeping and twisting about in a complete surrender to grief and frustration.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0043 }

“Goodness gracious!” Thirza puffed as she hurried out of the chamber. “It seems to me that the girl has lost her mind. A sane youth wouldn't act in the manner that she exhibits. If her mind is intact, her wickedness knows no bounds. Goodness me, my fear is that Agatha held the correct view all along. Nevertheless, having committed myself to this course, I shall not turn back.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0044 }

It was a gloomy morning. Thirza cleaned with intensity, scouring the shelves of the dairy and the porch floor whenever no other tasks presented themselves. Thirza required that labor, though it was unnecessary for either the porch or the shelves. After that, she stepped outside and cleared the yard with a rake.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0045 }

As soon as dinner was prepared, she walked over to the staircase to summon Nell. Over the banisters, a face marked with tears emerged, carrying a tragic expression.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0046 }

“Nell, come down and eat your dinner.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0047 }

“Thirza, I don’t want any dinner,” Nell said through her sobs. “Eating anything would be impossible for me. My heart has been broken. I anticipate that you will feel remorse of conscience for breaking it someday, Thirza, yet I forgive you. When that moment arrives, remember that I forgive you. However, please do not request that I eat anything, particularly boiled pork and greens. When a person is experiencing affliction, boiled pork and greens are so unromantic.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0048 }

Feeling exasperated, Thirza went back to the kitchen and shared her story of distress with Obed, who was rendered a wretched individual due to being torn between his devotion to justice and his illicit compassion for Nell.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0049 }

“Indeed, Thirza, taking the brooch was wrong of her, as was lying concerning it,” he conceded, gazing sorrowfully at his portion of mundane pork and vegetables as though he shared Nell’s view that such sustenance was inappropriate for emotional emergencies, “yet she is merely a child—and such a captivating child. Is it not rather harsh, in your opinion, to forbid her attending the outing when she desires it so greatly?”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0050 }

“Obed Abernethy, my mind is blown by your behavior. My belief is that I have treated her with far too much leniency. Furthermore, she does not seem to grasp the extent of her wickedness whatsoever—that remains my primary concern. Had she truly experienced remorse, the situation would not prove as severe. Nor do you appear to comprehend it either; you are constantly devising justifications for her in your mind—I am able to perceive that.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0051 }

“Well now, she is a tiny thing,” Obed weakly repeated. “And Thirza, you ought to make allowances. You are aware that she has not received any upbringing.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0052 }

“Well, it’s happening to her right now,” Thirza replied.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0053 }

Obed was struck mute by the reply, even though he remained unpersuaded. A profound gloom hung over that dinner. Tobias Buote, the hired boy, provided the sole bright spot, yet Thirza viewed his happy demeanor as a direct offense to her.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0054 }

Having completed the washing of her dishes, the setting of her bread sponge, and the feeding of her hens, Thirza recalled seeing a little tear in her finest black lace shawl upon removing it on Monday afternoon after coming home from the Ladies’ Aid.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0055 }

She intended to travel and repair it. Within a box inside her trunk rested the shawl. When Thirza extracted it, light from the sun, penetrating the dense vines grouped around the window, shone against an object trapped in the shawl—an object that gleamed and twinkled with facets of violet radiance. With a gasp, Thirza lunged for it. Suspended from a lace thread by its clasp, it was the amethyst brooch!
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0056 }

“Dear life and heart,” Thirza uttered expressionlessly, “what is the meaning of this? My brooch, which I believed was resting at the base of Pembroke’s pond, is right here unharmed. What was that girl’s reason for claiming she stole it and misplaced it? I assert that Grey Shutters must be under a spell. It comes back to me now that upon removing my shawl Monday afternoon, I placed it upon the bureau briefly. It seems the brooch became entangled in it in some way. Well!”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0057 }

With the brooch in her possession, Thirza made her way to the east gable. Having exhausted her tears, Nell sat beside the window in a state of dejection.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0058 }

“Nell Harcourt,” Thirza uttered in a serious tone, “my brooch was merely attached to my black lace shawl when I discovered it just now. Now, I desire an explanation for the rambling story you recounted to me earlier today.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0059 }

“Why, you told me I’d be held here until a confession was made,” Nell answered tiredly, “and therefore I chose to confess since reaching the picnic was something I had to do. Subsequent to going to bed last night, I devised a confession, making it just as engaging as possible. Furthermore, I repeated it repeatedly to ensure it remained in my memory. However, you refused to allow my attendance at the picnic anyway, meaning every bit of my effort went to waste.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0060 }

Thirza could not help laughing. Her conscience, however, stung her.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0061 }

“Nell, you really are something else! However, I was mistaken—I recognize that this moment. Having never known you to lie, I ought not to have disbelieved what you said. To be sure, admitting to something you were guiltless of was not correct—doing that was extremely wrong. Yet my actions forced you into it. Therefore, provided that you pardon me, Nell, I will pardon you, and we will begin anew on equal footing. Furthermore, prepare yourself now for the picnic.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0062 }

Nell launched upward with the speed of a rocket.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0063 }

“Oh, Thirza, is it not past the time?”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0064 }

“No, the time is merely two o'clock. Their assembly will hardly have begun, and tea will not be served for another hour. Clean your face, brush your hair, and dress in your gingham. I am going to pack a basket on your behalf. We have an abundance of baked goods in the dwelling. Furthermore, I will have Tobias harness the sorrel horse to take you down to the location of the picnic.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0065 }

“Oh, Thirza,” Nell cried out, rushing over to the washstand. “A mere five minutes back I felt so wretched that I wished I had not been born, but at this moment I would not trade positions with an angel!”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0066 }

When night fell, Nell went back to Grey Shutters utterly content and entirely exhausted, experiencing an indescribable condition of beatitude.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0067 }

“Oh, Thirza, my time was absolutely scrumptious. Today I picked up that brand-new word, scrumptious. Mary Alice Bell was using it when I overheard her. Doesn't it convey a lot? All of it was delightful. A wonderful tea was served to us, after which Mr. Gorham Pullen brought everyone out rowing on the Lake of Glassy Waters, taking six people per trip. Then Odette Pullen almost tumbled into the water. As she reached far out to gather water lilies, Mr. Pullen managed to grab her sash right at the critical moment, preventing her from falling in and likely drowning. My preference would have been for that to happen to me. Being almost drowned would have made for such a romantic adventure. What an exciting story it would make to relate. Plus, there was ice cream for us. That ice cream is beyond my ability to depict with words. Thirza, I guarantee you that it was divine.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0068 }

That night, while working on her stocking basket, Thirza recounted the entire tale to Obed.
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0069 }

“I am ready to admit my error,” she finished frankly, “yet I have gained some wisdom. Thinking about the ‘confession’ Nell made brings a laugh to me, even if I ought not to smile since it truly amounted to an untruth. Somehow, though, it feels less terrible than the alternative would have proved, and regardless, the blame for it lies with me. Certain sides of that child are difficult to comprehend. Nevertheless, my faith remains that she will turn out fine in the end. One fact is beyond doubt, however: any home containing her will never suffer from boredom.”
{: #nw-v01-c14-p0070 }
